In March, Welsh Finance Secretary Mark Drakeford stated it would constitute a "democratic outrage" if London ministers attempted to block the Welsh Trade Union Bill. The Labour Welsh Government contends that UK ministers shouldn't enforce restrictions on union activities within Wales' devolved services, such as healthcare and education. The committee's report lacked unanimous support, as Conservative AM Janet Finch-Saunders dissented from the other seven members.

Evha Jannath, aged 11, fell from a circular boat on the Splash Canyon ride at Drayton Manor during a school trip on Tuesday. Following this incident, several theme parks including Alton Towers and Legoland Windsor have temporarily closed similar water-based thrill rides. Drayton Manor announced it would remain closed on Friday to allow for health and safety investigations. According to a spokesperson from Merlin Entertainments, which operates Legoland and Alton Towers, their comparable attractions were shut down "with immediate effect" on a "precautionary basis" after learning about Tuesday's fatal accident. Merlin Entertainments anticipates reopening these rides on Friday. However, not all venues have taken similar precautions - Lightwater Valley in North Yorkshire and West Midland Safari Park have kept their similar attractions operational despite the tragedy at Drayton Manor.

Rangers secured the Challenge Cup trophy on their fourth attempt with a convincing victory. Ally Gilchrist's early own goal and James Tavernier's powerful shot established an insurmountable advantage. The Championship winners added further goals through Andy Halliday's penalty and Kenny Miller's close-range finish. Mark Warburton's team now prepares to face Celtic, the Premiership leaders, in the Scottish Cup semi-final at Hampden Park next Sunday. Rangers had previously struggled in this tournament, suffering defeats to Queen of the South, Raith Rovers, and Alloa Athletic in its various formats. The playing surface at the national stadium drew criticism, as both Rangers and League One side Peterhead competed on a pitch that was hardly suitable. Despite being installed at a cost of £200,000 just over a month ago, the field will be replaced before the upcoming semi-final due to failure to properly settle. The part-time Peterhead team entered the match as significant underdogs at odds of 22-1.

Members of the Royal College of Midwives (RCM) plan to strike for four hours, following a 9-1 vote in favor of industrial action—the first such decision in the organization's 134-year history. The Department of Health expressed disappointment but committed to working with trusts to maintain safe services for mothers and babies, stating their door remains open for talks. The RCM is seeking urgent discussions with the health minister to resolve the dispute. According to RCM NI director Bredagh Hughes, midwives are requesting the same 1% pay increase received by their counterparts in Wales, Scotland and England. "It is crucial that women understand this dispute is not with or about them, but with the department of health and employers," she explained. "No woman will be put at risk, as full emergency coverage will be provided, and midwives on the picket line will be available to step in if needed."

The World Half Marathon on Saturday, March 26 will feature approximately 200 elite athletes and up to 25,000 recreational runners completing a 13.1-mile course. Beginning at Cardiff Castle and concluding on King Edward VII Avenue in the city center, the route has earned praise from former 10,000m world record holder Dave Bedford: "It's a great course—flat and showcasing Cardiff at its best, both historic and impressively modern." Participants will pass numerous landmarks including the Millennium Stadium, Cardiff City Stadium, Penarth Marina, Cardiff Bay Barrage, Wales Millennium Centre, and Roath Park Lake before finishing in the heart of the Welsh capital. This marks Wales' first time hosting these championships. With Cardiff organizing annual half marathons since 2003, officials hope this world-class event will further enhance the city's reputation as a premier racing destination, especially with the involvement of double Olympic gold medalists.

This new status represents the end of an era for the site, which was utilized for heavy industry for nearly 200 years until its central colliery closed in 1983. Portions of the area had previously received recognition for their environmental significance. Despite the company potentially benefiting from the approved plan, the 72-year-old Conservative councillor will retain his public office position. The Bournemouth Magistrates' Court district judge determined Flower, a Verwood resident, had violated Localism Act 2011 regulations. He received a six-month conditional discharge and was ordered to pay £930 in costs. Following the ruling, Flower expressed surprise and disappointment at being found guilty "on a technicality," noting the court imposed "the lowest possible penalty" while emphasizing there was "total lack of any personal gain or intent." When approached outside court, he declined to comment on his political future.

UN Envoy Sigrid Kaag reported that Syria appears to have missed a Sunday deadline to remove its chemical arsenal from the country. The complete destruction of Syria's chemical weapons is scheduled by June 30th. The plan to eliminate Syria's arsenal was established through a Russian-US agreement last year following a deadly sarin rocket attack near Damascus that killed hundreds. The operation to dispose of these weapons is jointly supervised by the UN Security Council and the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW). While the final UN deadline for destroying Syria's chemical weapons remains June 30th, Syria had committed to completing the removal of its stockpile by April 27th after failing to meet earlier deadlines. "Most of the chemical weapons material has been removed but not yet destroyed, which applies to the June 30th deadline. That's why removing the remaining chemical weapons material from the one site is so crucial," stated Ms. Kaag, who heads the OPCW-UN mission.
